free_text: The patient is a 73-year-old male with a high PSA of 113.0 ng/mL and a biopsy-confirmed Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5) prostate adenocarcinoma with perineural invasion. MRI shows a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone base, with a clinical T stage of cT2a. Management requires clinical review of individual treatment benefit given the high-grade disease and local extension findings.
